title: Read-only storage migration comms scratch
content:
Context and purpose:
- Quick personal scratchpad for announcing a planned read-only window for user artifacts during the storage migration (thin slice of objects: logs/legacy-checkpoints).
- Goal: minimize surprise; provide engineers and support with exact language; provide a short customer-facing blurb and escalation map.
- Migration window likely to be 90 minutes; tentative date: 2026-03-18 02:00-03:30 UTC. Final timing depends on infra dry run on 2026-03-15 (INFR-1987).

High-level headline (one-liner to use in announcements):
- Short internal: "Planned read-only window for historical artifacts — minimal user impact, short interruption to write operations"
- Short customer-facing: "Planned maintenance: temporary read-only mode for older artifacts. Reads will continue, writes to legacy artifact paths will be rejected for ~90 minutes while we migrate storage to the new durable cluster."

Draft internal announcement (Slack / all-hands note):
- Subject/Title: Planned read-only window for legacy artifact migration (tentative 2026-03-18 02:00 UTC)
- Body (bullet-friendly):
  * What: We'll place the legacy artifact namespace into read-only to migrate objects to the new durable cluster. This affects writes to the legacy paths only (not model inference or API request payloads).
  * When: Tentative window 2026-03-18 02:00-03:30 UTC (90 minutes). Final timing after dry run on 2026-03-15.
  * Impact: Reads should continue as normal. Attempts to write new artifacts (uploads, legacy checkpoint writes, archival requests) will receive a 409/451-style error indicating read-only mode. API endpoints for inference/hosted API unaffected.
  * Why: We need to move a small but high-risk dataset to the new cluster to reduce tail latency and improve durability for customers on older flows.
  * Who to notify externally: Customer Success + 2x EILCs for any accounts with ongoing long-running uploads.
  * Rollback: If any critical error, we will abort migration and bring namespace back to read-write; fallback plan includes quick redirect back to old storage gateway.

All-hands 90-second talking points (for on-stage drop-in):
- "Short update: we'll run a targeted migration next week that requires read-only on a small set of legacy artifacts for ~90 minutes. This is low-risk and won't affect runtime inference. Customer Success, Support, and SRE have playbooks ready. We'll post final timing after the dry run on Monday."
- "Why it matters: this reduces rare tail failures and will simplify future maintenance. We ran the tests and expect >95% zero-impact for customer-facing flows."
- "Ask to engineering: be available for a 2-hour window after the migration in case of edge-case followups; we may need quick fixes to artifact routing logic."

Customer-facing FAQ (short, to be reviewed by CS/legal):
- Q: Will my app be down?
  A: No — inference endpoints and most customer reads remain available. Only writes to older artifact namespaces will be blocked during the short window.
- Q: Will data be lost?
  A: No — migration is a copy-then-swap; we validate checksums before switching. We also keep a temporary snapshot for 48 hours after migration.
- Q: How will I know when it's done?
  A: We will post a status update in the status page (status.redwood.ai) and send customer notifications to accounts that attempted writes in that window.
- Q: Does this affect Dedicated/Private deployments?
  A: Hosted clusters only. Customers on Private deployments are unaffected unless they explicitly requested migration support.

Support playbook (concise):
- Expected symptoms: 409/430-ish errors on artifact write, client retries that timeout, users opening support tickets about failed uploads.
- First response template (Slack snippet):
  "Thanks for flagging — we are running a planned short maintenance that temporarily blocks writes to legacy artifacts. Reads are unaffected. We're tracking your ticket and will confirm completion as soon as the migration completes (ETA ~90 min)."
- Escalation steps:
  1) Triage in #support-ops, tag SRE oncall.
  2) If >10 customers across accounts report failed writes, notify CS lead + incident commander.
  3) If any long-running upload is at risk (customer flagged), pause migration and run per-account remediation (INFR-1987-subtask).

Engineering checklist (pre-migration):
- Run full dry-run with subset of data 2026-03-15 (owner: Mateo Chen).
- Confirm read-only toggle works and returns the correct error payload (404 vs 409 semantics).
- Prepare rollback commands and test restore to read-write in staging.
- Ensure status page automation is ready to update.

Slack templates (short):
- Public channel update: "Heads up — planned short read-only window for legacy artifacts on 2026-03-18 02:00 UTC. Reads continue; writes to legacy paths will be rejected for ~90m. Link to status doc: <confluence link>"
- DM to CS about specific accounts: "We plan to run migration during X. Account <acct> has an open long-running upload — recommend pausing their job or we can coordinate a short maintenance window. Ping if you'd like exec-level note."

Edge cases / unknowns (notes to self):
- Some SDKs may surface ambiguous error messages; we need a small mapping blog post for SDK teams explaining how to surface a friendly message.
- Observability: ensure logs contain a migration-id and short traceable tag to link failed writes back to the migration job.
- Compliance: confirm retention snapshot policy with security (Rina).

Draft customer notification (short email/snippet):
- Subject: Planned maintenance: temporary write suspension for legacy artifacts
- Body (short): "We are performing a planned migration to improve reliability. During the maintenance window (2026-03-18 02:00-03:30 UTC), attempts to write older artifacts may fail. Reads and inference are not impacted. We'll send a confirmation when complete. If you're performing long-running uploads, please pause or contact your CS rep."

Next steps (action items):
- [ ] Finalize migration dry-run and measure error surface (owner: Mateo) — due 2026-03-15
- [ ] Lock final migration window and publish to status page — owner: Asha — target 2026-03-16
- [ ] Coordinate CS outbound to top-50 affected customers — owner: Rina — target 2026-03-16
- [ ] Prepare support canned replies and create a dedicated triage board (support) — owner: Alex (support)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep language upbeat: emphasize shortness, read-only vs full outage, copy-then-swap guarantees.
- Avoid technical overload in customer-facing notes — save checksum/validation details for CS/technical docs.
- If dry run shows >5% failure rate for SDK uploads, escalate to PM for postponement.

Raw draft for quick paste into Slack #eng-platform: 
"Planned read-only migration to move legacy artifacts to new cluster. Tentative: 2026-03-18 02:00-03:30 UTC. Reads unaffected; writes to legacy paths blocked for ~90m. Dry run on 2026-03-15. Contact Asha or Mateo with urgent questions"

End of scratchpad.

Revision history (personal):
- 2026-03-10: initial notes, rough timeline
- 2026-03-12: added customer FAQ + support playbook + owners

-- Asha
